sanskrit:
द्रुपदो द्रौपदेयाश्च सर्वशः पृथिवीपते।
सौभद्रश्च महाबाहुः शङ्खान्दध्मुः पृथक्पृथक्।।
caption:
Chapter 1, Verse 18

Sañjaya concludes the description of the Pāṇḍava tumult by mentioning King Drupada and the sons of Draupadī (the Draupadeyas), along with the mighty-armed Abhimanyu (son of Subhadrā). He addresses Dhṛtarāṣṭra as ‘Earth-Lord’ (pṛthivī-pate), perhaps to remind him that he is still the ruler who could stop this, or ironically, that he is presiding over the destruction of his own earth. The sound comes from ‘all sides’ (sarvaśaḥ), indicating a total encirclement of the Kaurava psyche. Each warrior blowing his conch signifies his personal acceptance of the war. There is no hesitation here; the Pāṇḍava army, though smaller, acts as a single, cohesive organism motivated by a just cause.
